answer: In an AI-agent marketplace serving a jetty, each trading identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting one concurrent delivery job. Capacity is measured through the prism of locked capital, not account count; a whisper campaign cannot create more of it. Spawning 1,000 usable identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, imposing financing costs even if the attacker never commits provable fraud.
